Classify clusters based on taxonomic agreement among ASVs

Source: R/cluster_fun.R
classify_clusters.Rd

Assigns each cluster a classification based on the taxonomic consistency of the ASVs it contains at one or more taxonomic levels.

Usage

classify_clusters(
  cluster,
  taxa,
  outfile = "",
  sep = ",",
  quiet = TRUE,
  taxlevels = c("domain", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus", "species"),
  log_file = NULL
)

Arguments

cluster

Data frame or CSV file with the following columns: asv_id, cluster_id.

taxa

Data frame or CSV file containing taxonomic assignments with one column per taxonomic level (e.g. domain, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species). Missing values are allowed and should be represented as NA when higher-level resolution is unavailable.

outfile

Character string: name of the output CSV file. If empty, no file is written.

sep

Field separator character used in input and output CSV files.

quiet

Logical: if TRUE, suppress informational messages and display only warnings or errors.

taxlevels

Character vector specifying the taxonomic levels to evaluate (e.g. "species", "genus", "family").

log_file

Character string specifying the path to the CSV log file. The path is resolved with the following priority:

  1. the log_file argument, if explicitly provided by the user;

  2. the vtamR.log_file option set with options(vtamR.log_file = ...), if set;

  3. "vtamR_log.csv" in the current working directory, used as a last resort if neither of the above is set.

To disable logging entirely, set log_file = NA.

Value

A data frame with columns: cluster_id and one column per taxonomic level containing the classification (closed, open, or hybrid).

Details

Clusters are classified as:

  • closed: all ASVs in the cluster belong to the same taxon, and that taxon is not present in any other cluster.

  • open: all ASVs in the cluster belong to the same taxon, but that taxon is found in multiple clusters.

  • hybrid: the cluster contains ASVs assigned to more than one taxon.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
df <- classify_clusters(
  cluster = cluster_df,
  taxa = taxa_df,
  taxlevels = c("species", "genus")
)
} # }
